learning_outcomes.text: The student recognizes the constant and variable elements of the functioning of social groups, individuals and organizations and is able to determine their mutual relations and influence on the behavior between the group and the individual.
The student uses the knowledge obtained in the framework of various modules to evaluate the non-technical effects of engineering activities and adopt responsible attitudes.

The student defines the rules of managing people in groups and teams. The student knows and is able to apply the principles of leadership and motivation. The student understands the need to update their knowledge and is able to identify and use the sources of knowledge. The student knows the principles of Continuing Improvement and the benefits of skilful use of the potential of human resources in terms of creativity and innovation.

syllabus_topics: Short history of sociology. Main traditions: functionalism, symbolic interactionism, conflict theory.
Basic sociological concepts: social control, institiutions, social roles.
Methodology of sociology: quantitive and qualitative methods, social network analysis.
Sociology of scientific knowledge: from positivism to the strong programme.
Science and technology studies: actor-network theory
Economic sociology: sociological tools in economic analysis.
Sociology of culture: socialization, mass media, gender.
assessment_rules: The passing threshold for the test is 60.0%.
bibliography: Peter L. Berger, Invitation to sociology: a humanistic perspective, Harmondsworth: Penguin, 1966.
Kathleen Odell Korgen (ed.), The Cambridge Handbook of Sociology, Vol 1. Core Areas in Sociology and the Development of the Discipline. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2017.
Jonathan H. Turner (ed.), Handbook of Sociological Theory, New York: Springer, 2001.
Neil J. Smelser, Richard Swedberg, The Handbook of Economic Sociology, Princeton University Press, 2005.
John R. Hall, Laura Grindstaff, Ming-cheng Lo, Handbook of Cultural Sociology, Routledge, 2010.
degree: Mechanical Engineering, first-cycle (engineer), specialization Design and Production Engineering
